text: I. Framework of Professional Core CoursesPharmacy is a comprehensive discipline that studies the discovery, development, preparation, evaluation and clinical application of drugs. Its curriculum system is based on "chemistry as the foundation, biology as the background, pharmacology as the core, and pharmaceutical administration as the guarantee", and is specifically divided into the following modules:Ii. Basic Medicine and Life Science Courses1. Medical foundation categoryHuman anatomy and physiology: Systematically study the structure and physiological functions of human organs (such as the circulatory system and nervous system), laying a foundation for understanding the targets of drug action.Pathophysiology: Analyzing the mechanisms of disease occurrence and development (such as inflammation and tumor pathology), and helping to master the pathological basis of drug treatment.Biochemistry: It studies the structure and metabolism of biological macromolecules such as proteins and nucleic acids, and explains the interaction between drugs and biomolecules (such as enzyme inhibition mechanisms).2. Biology and MicrobiologyCell biology: Understanding the effects of drugs on cell proliferation and apoptosis at the cellular level (such as the mechanism of action of anti-cancer drugs).Microbiology and Immunology: Study the characteristics of pathogenic microorganisms and human immune responses, covering the principles of antibiotic development and vaccine preparation.Iii. Chemistry and Medicinal Chemistry Courses
